description: What the interact key does by a prop, and which one thing it acts on (PL.examine-props, U49(3); the Unreal P8 critic's m1 and its collision with P6's E actions): each stated prop (entities.props) has one meaning, read_sign, examine, open_board or none; what reading and examining say and raise; where the notice board is posted; and, where the player stands, the one target E acts on among a talk villager, pick-ups, containers, the board, a door and the props. Ops: noun {archetypes} -> {nouns}; meanings {props, board? | settlement?} -> {board, meanings, count}; host {props, settlement} -> {host}; interact {props | prop, board? | settlement?} -> {results: [{id, ok, action, line, events} | {id, ok: false, refusal}]}; target {at, panel?, villager?, pickups?, containers?, buildings?, props?, board? | settlement?, ranges?, stands?: [{name, at, ...overrides}]} -> {ok, target} | {ok: false, refusal} (with stands: {board, stands: [{at, ok, target}]}). board is {host, name}; given a settlement instead, the board is posted by host and named for it. Every case is {name, op, input, expected}; numbers compare within tolerance, everything else exactly, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent). Runner: src/props/props-corpus.ts. Regenerate with npm run props-corpora; npm run props-corpora:check fails on any difference.

contract.segments: an archetype is under a key when it equals the key or starts with the key and a dot (whole dotted segments)
contract.meaning: no archetype -> none (no_archetype); under notOffered -> none (built_fabric); the board host -> open_board, prompt "Read the <name> notice board" (no name: "Read the notice board"); under signArchetypes -> read_sign, prompt "Read the sign"; else examine, prompt "Examine the <noun>". One meaning per prop: the board host is never read as a sign; a prop.container.* prop is examined, never opened (only a ContainerIR opens)
contract.noun: split the archetype on dots, dropping empty segments; fewer than three -> object; the fourth segment and the third ("produce stall") when there are four or more and the fourth is longer than one letter, else the third; underscores read as spaces
contract.text: the prop's text trimmed; empty or absent is none
contract.host: of the props under signArchetypes and not under notOffered, with a finite position, that do not state a settlementId other than the settlement's: the nearest to the settlement's position on the ground plane, the first listed on a tie; none -> null (no board is posted); a settlement with no finite position -> null
contract.read: read_sign: line "The sign reads: <text>", or "The sign is blank." with no text; events [sign_read {signId: id, objectId: id, targetText: text or '', nativeText: the same}] and nothing else (an object_examined beside it would complete the tutorial's next lesson in the same press)
contract.examine: examine: line "You examine the <noun>." or, with text, "You examine the <noun>: <text>" plus a full stop unless the text ends in . ! or ?; events [object_examined {objectId: id, objectName: noun, targetWord: '', targetLanguage: ''}] (no word: the language tracker records nothing, as for any untranslated object)
contract.board: open_board: line null, events []: the board model (notice-board.json) takes over
contract.notOfferedResult: interact on a prop with no meaning is refused not_offered (field archetype, with its reason)
contract.target: at not a finite point -> bad_position. An open panel (a non-empty panel) -> close_panel. Else the actions tier: the villager the host would talk to (talk, "Talk to <name or id>"), each pick-up not taken ("Pick up <name or id>"), each container ("Open the <label, ASCII A-Z folded to a-z; none: container>"), the board host prop ("Read the <name> notice board"), each within its range compared with <=, and the door doorPrompt gives (outside, "Enter <label>"): the nearest on the ground plane wins, a tie going in actionTier order and then to the first listed. Only when no action is in range, the looking tier: each prop read or examined within its range, the nearest, the first listed on a tie. Nothing -> null. A candidate with no id or no finite position is skipped. distance is metres rounded to 1e-9; the prompt is the words after the host's key glyph
contract.ranges: ranges overrides any of rangesM per call; a door prompts by doorPrompt alone
contract.notHere: inside an interior (doorPrompt's exit) and a conversation in progress are the host's and not this rule's; the language world's translated objects are examineNearest's (world-words.ts)

deviations.why: pipelines states a fence panel along every front yard with room for one (settlement-dressing.ts), the same built fabric as a wall

deviations.unreal: the board is posted on the sign nearest the settlement centre (P6) and the same sign is "Read the sign" (P8): one prop, two meanings
deviations.core: the board host prop means open_board only and raises no sign_read; every other sign is read
deviations.why: one key press has one meaning per prop; the board is what P6 already made E do there

deviations.unreal: P6: a pick-up, container, board or door strictly nearer than the talk villager wins, else talk; P8: talk when a villager is in range, else the nearest prop
deviations.core: one rule: the actions tier (talk, pick-up, container, board, door) by nearest, then the looking tier (sign, examine) only when no action is in range
deviations.why: the two interim rules disagree once both land; a pick-up settled 1 m from a barrel must be picked up

deviations.unreal: PropsTargetNear considers a prompting door at the player's own location (distance 0), so it beats every other target in range
deviations.core: a door competes at doorPrompt's distance
deviations.why: the nearest rule; no Brightwater door prompts (all no_interior), so nothing live changes

deviations.unreal: PropToInteract keeps the LAST prop at an equal distance (D <= BestD)

deviations.core: whole dotted segments: the archetype is the key or starts with the key and a dot

deviations.unreal: PropNoun: the third segment, or "<fourth> <third>" when the fourth is longer than one letter; fewer than three segments is "object"
deviations.core: the same, with underscores read as spaces
deviations.why: a key segment like notice_board reads "notice board" in a prompt

deviations.unreal: a stated prop with no archetype is "Examine the object"

deviations.unreal: "You examine the <noun>: <text>." always adds a full stop
deviations.core: no full stop is added after text that already ends in . ! or ?
deviations.why: a stated text with its own punctuation would read "..": no Brightwater text ends in one

deviations.unreal: the board host is chosen from every stated sign, for the first settlement only
deviations.core: a sign that states another settlementId is not considered for this settlement's board
deviations.why: a world with two settlements posts each board in its own settlement; Brightwater has one
